# Phase 1 and Phase 7 move the upstream design to Planned; no flag is on either
# call line.
# Every record here is `always`, and the absence of a mode-scoped record is a
# recorded finding rather than an oversight. /plan selects single-pr or multi-pr
# at step 3.6 of phase-3-decomposition.md, which is exactly where a mode call
# would go; that step says in prose that /plan makes none, and this is the other
# half of the same statement.
# gh is always rather than mode:multi-pr because Resume Logic checks for
# existing issues with `gh issue list --search` on every run, before the
# execution mode is known. Issue creation, labelling, and milestone work in
# Phase 7 multi-pr add more gh subcommands but no new tool -- and gh has an
# independent release cadence, so its record names the tool alone and multi-pr
# cannot change what verifying it means.
# jq backs build-dependency-graph.sh (Phase 5), create-issues-batch.sh, and the
# outline-envelope read in plan-to-tasks.sh; git backs the Phase 7 wip-hygiene
# scan and the same script's repo-root resolution.
# `shirabe validate --lifecycle-chain` is a call /plan makes: Phase 7 runs it
# over the finished PLAN to decide whether the upstream is at a status a PLAN
# may be built from. That check used to live in skills/plan/scripts/validate-plan.sh,
# which is why python3 (its portable realpath) was declared here; the script is
# gone and the validator owns the rule, so the record went with it.
# The `shirabe validate --lifecycle` line in SKILL.md describes the CI
# workflow, which /plan does not run. Nothing mechanical separates that
# documentation from a call site, so it is exempted by name for
# scripts/check-skill-requires.sh; an exemption that stops matching its line
# fails as stale.
